title: De Broglie Ratio
q_prose: A proton and an alpha particle are accelerated from rest to the same kinetic energy. Find the ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths.
q_reminder: Find lambda p to lambda alpha.
q_narration: A proton and an alpha particle start from rest and are accelerated so that both have the same kinetic energy. We have to compare their de Broglie wavelengths. Let us solve step by step.

steps.label: Step 1 — Use de Broglie formula
steps.narration: The de Broglie wavelength is Planck constant divided by momentum. For a particle starting from rest with kinetic energy, momentum is root of two m K.

steps.label: Step 2 — Combine the relations
steps.narration: So, for the same kinetic energy, the wavelength depends inversely on the square root of mass.

steps.label: Step 3 — Write wavelength ratio
steps.narration: Now take the ratio of proton wavelength to alpha particle wavelength. The constants cancel out.

steps.label: Step 4 — Substitute masses and energy
steps.narration: Both kinetic energies are equal, and an alpha particle has four times the mass of a proton. Hence the ratio becomes square root of four, which is two.

answer_narration: So the proton wavelength is twice the alpha particle wavelength, giving two is to one. Correct option A. For more clear practice, keep learning with Acharya.
